chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“There is no harm in the muhrim changing his clothes; however, when he enters Makkah, he should wear the two garments of his ihram in which he entered ihram, and it is disliked that he sell them.”
And a concession permitting their sale has also been narrated.

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: he entered into the state of ihram
key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: his state or garments of ihram
key_terms.بَيْعِهِمَا: the sale of the two garments
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred destination of pilgrimage
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim change his clothes and sell his ihram garments?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the clothing of a muhrim during ihram. It states that changing clothes is permissible, recommends wearing the original two ihram garments upon entering Makkah, and indicates that selling those garments is disliked, though another report allows it.
